scope: DCP-LETT-1670 and preserved Blyth/Darwin candidates in reports/1851-1855/review/all_letters.jsonl

record_reviews.date_assessment: Dated 21 April 1855 at Calcutta, with an exact XML when date. It acknowledges Darwin's 27 February letter, but the outgoing Darwin letter itself is not preserved in the searched pool. The page has a separate CD annotation/abstract section; that later editorially exposed note is not evidence that Darwin wrote the note on 21 April.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: The 13 body paragraphs are Edward Blyth's prose, ending with his promise to send a Jungle cock skeleton. The salutation 'My dear Sir,' is excluded. Blyth discusses domestic races, dogs, cats, hybrids, silkworms, birds and cattle, and asks Darwin to send tame peafowl legs; the body is not a Darwin response.
record_reviews.summary: Blyth opens by acknowledging receipt of Darwin's 27 February letter and the subject of variation in domestic animals. He then supplies a long sequence of concrete observations: introduced and local dogs, possible wolf/dog continuities, Indian cat forms, silk-worm generations, domestic geese and cattle, hybrid fertility, and regional bird variation. The final paragraph promises a Jungle cock skeleton. This is a substantive incoming source, but its corresponding Darwin question letter is unlocated and its text does not quote or identify a later Darwin reply.
record_reviews.candidate_status: incoming_evidence_only; no identified Darwin response endpoint

evidence.quote: I have the pleasure to acknowledge receipt of yours of the 27th. February, and am much gratified to learn that a subject in which I have always felt the deepest interest has been undertaken by one so competent to treat of it in all its bearings.
I will send you a Jungle cock skeleton by first opportunity

record_reviews.date_assessment: Dated 4 August 1855 at Calcutta with an exact XML when date. It explicitly records receipt of Darwin's 18 June letter and refers to Blyth's earlier 20 April epistle, but does not state that the 20 April item is the catalogue's 21 April 1670 record; that identification remains a one-day/date discrepancy and cannot be circularly assumed.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: All surviving body paragraphs are Blyth's, including his answers to Darwin's queries and his reports of local observations. The salutation 'My dear Sir,' is excluded. Footnotes identify later editorial sources and Darwin's separate abstracts; they are not additional contemporary Darwin prose.
record_reviews.summary: This later Blyth letter is the strongest preserved witness for an exchange following the 1670-era correspondence. Its opening says Darwin's 18 June letter had arrived and that the earlier 20 April epistle supplied useful hints; it then answers queries about trained otters, rabbits, canaries, geese, cats and pigeons and discusses Darwin's domestic-animal investigation. It establishes a later Darwin-to-Blyth response and Blyth's receipt of that response, but the searched collection contains no body of Darwin's 18 June letter and no exact phrase tying that outgoing to every subject in 1670.
record_reviews.candidate_status: later incoming witness; supports exchange continuity, not a direct 1670 response pair

evidence.quote: I have now had the pleasure of receiving yours of the 18th. June, & am gratified to learn from it that my long and desultory epistle of the 20th. April has supplied a few useful hints.
Now for your queries; but firstly, need I remark how utterly astounded I felt to learn about Dixon!

candidate_comparison.assessment: Actual Blyth-to-Darwin body with an explicit reference to Darwin's 18 June outgoing and Blyth's 20 April epistle. It is a dated later witness, not the missing Darwin response to 1670, and the 20/21 April identification is not proven by proximity.

A later joint Bashford/Blyth memorandum about silkworm crosses, dated after 3 July 1855. It contains distinct Bashford observations and a Blyth forwarding note, but no reference identifying 1670 or a Darwin response to it; it is not a substitute endpoint.

A 22–23 August 1855 Blyth letter with quoted Thomas Hutton answers and separate Blyth notes. It continues Darwin's domestic-animal questions but is later and cross-voice; no wording identifies it as the response to 1670.

findings: No preserved Darwin-to-Blyth body dated 27 February 1855 or 18 June 1855 was found in the searched all_letters pool; only Blyth's acknowledgements survive.
1735 proves Blyth received a Darwin letter dated 18 June and regarded his earlier 20 April epistle as useful, but it does not establish a direct 1670-to-Darwin reply pair.

1670 should remain incoming evidence with its exact 21 April date and broad domestic-animal scope; any Darwin knowledge or response scope requires the missing outgoing source or a more explicit later witness.
missing_or_unresolved: Darwin's 27 February 1855 letter acknowledged in 1670 is absent from the searched preserved pool.
Darwin's 18 June 1855 letter acknowledged in 1735 is absent from the searched preserved pool.
The relationship between Blyth's '20th. April' epistle in 1735 and catalogue record 1670 (21 April) is unresolved; no circular date or topic inference is used.
